title: Seq-Well: portable, low-cost RNA sequencing of single cells at high throughput
protocol: Place a pre-cut (22 x 66 mm) polycarbonate membrane onto a glass slide using tweezers and a gloved finger.
Discard any membranes that have creases or other large-scale imperfections.
Place membranes onto a shelf in the plasma cleaner, preferably on the bottom shelf to reduce risk of them flying after vacuum is removed.
Close the plasma cleaner door and turn on the main power and pump switch.
Ensure the 3-way valve lever is at the 9:00 position before forming the vacuum.
Allow the vacuum to form for 2 minutes.
Simultaneously turn the valve to 12:00 while turning the power to the Hi setting once the vacuum has formed.
Treat membranes with plasma for 7 minutes.
Turn the RF level valve from HIGH to OFF after treatment.
Turn off the power followed by turning off the vacuum.
Slowly open the valve until you can barely hear air entering chamber.
Leave until the door opens (~5 min).
Remove slides from plasma cleaner and transfer to a 4-well dish.
If membranes have slightly folded over, slowly flip the membrane back using needle nose tweezers.
If membranes have blown off the slide entirely, repeat above procedure to ensure you know which side was exposed to plasma.
Quickly pipette 5 mL of 1xPBS over the dry membrane.
Gently hydrate one end of the membrane with a single drop so that it adheres to the slide before dispensing the entire volume.
Remove any air bubbles underneath the membrane using wafer forceps.
Membranes are now functionalized and ready for use.
Solvate membranes with 1xPBS if they need to be used within 48 hours.
If transporting solvated membranes, remove all but ~1 mL of PBS.
Alternatively, dry out membranes after solvation in 1xPBS and store at room temperature for up to 4 weeks.
Rehydrate stored membranes with 1xPBS when ready to use.
Aspirate the storage solution from arrays and solvate them with 5 mL of bead loading buffer \(BLB).
Place arrays under vacuum with rotation \(50 RPM) for 10-15 minutes to remove air bubbles in wells.
Aliquot ~110,000 beads from stock into a 1.5 mL tube.
Spin the tube on a tabletop centrifuge for 10-15 seconds to form a pellet.
Aspirate storage buffer and wash beads once with 500 μL of BLB.
Pellet beads.
Aspirate BLB.
Resuspend beads in 200 μL of BLB.
Thoroughly aspirate BLB from the dish containing the array(s).
Do not aspirate or dry the PDMS surface of the array(s).
Use a 200 μL pipette to apply 200 μL containing 110,000 beads drop-wise to the surface of each array.
Place the loaded array(s) onto a rotator for 10 minutes at 75 RPM.
Thoroughly wash array(s) to remove excess beads from the surface.
Position each array so that it sits in the center of the 4-well dish.
Dispense 500 μL of BLB in the upper right corner of each array and 500 μL in the bottom right corner of each array.
Be careful not to directly pipette onto the microwells.
Push each array against the left side of the 4-well dish using wafer forceps to create a capillary flow for removing beads from the surface.
Aspirate the liquid, reposition each array, and repeat on the opposite side.
Examine the arrays periodically under a microscope to ensure no loose beads are present.
Once excess beads have been removed, solvate each array with 5 mL of BLB.
If continuing cell loading within 1-5 hours, store loaded arrays in 5 mL of BLB.
For storage up to 72 hours, keep loaded arrays in Array Quenching Buffer.
Obtain a cell or tissue sample.
Prepare a single cell suspension using your preferred protocol.
Aspirate the BLB from each array and soak it in 5 mL of RPMI + 10% FBS for 5 minutes.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Make a new solution of 10,000 cells in 200 μL of RP-10.
Aspirate the RP-10 and center each array in a well.
Load the cell loading solution dropwise onto the surface of each array.
Intermittently rock the array(s) in the x & y direction for 5 minutes.
Wash arrays 4 times with 5 mL of PBS to remove FBS from media.
Aspirate final PBS wash and replace with 5 mL of RPMI media (no FBS).
When pre-imaging cells, load cells first before beads.
Count cells using a hemocytometer and resuspend 10,000 cells in 200 μL of cold CellCover.
Incubate cells at 4°C for 1 hour.
Perform antibody staining on fixed cells at 4°C.
Wash cells twice with 1xPBS.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL of CellCover10 buffer and place on ice.
Soak array(s) with 5 mL of CellCover10 buffer.
Aspirate media and load fixed cells onto the array(s) dropwise.
Gently rock the array(s) in the x & y direction for 5 minutes.
Wash arrays twice with 5 mL of CellCover10 (pH 10 + 10% FBS).
Solvate arrays in 5 mL of CellCover (No FBS).
Place a lift slip on each array and image with a microscope.
After imaging, wash each array in 5 mL of CellCover10 media.
Immediately load beads using the bead loading protocol provided above.
Use the wafer forceps to transfer the array from media to the lid of a 4-well dish.
Use the wafer forceps to remove a pre-treated membrane from the 4-well dish.
Gently dab away moisture from the glass slide on the paper towel until the membrane does not spontaneously change position on the glass slide.
Carefully position the membrane on the center of the microscope slide, leaving a small (2-3 mm) membrane overhang beyond the edge of the slide.
Holding the membrane in your left hand, invert the microscope slide so that the treated surface is facing down.
Place the overhang of the membrane in contact with the PDMS surface of the array just above the boundary of the microwells.
Firmly hold down the overhang of the membrane against the PDMS surface of the array with your right hand.
While maintaining pressure with your right hand to hold the membrane in place, gently apply the membrane with your left hand.
After applying the membrane, carefully pry the array and membrane from the surface of the lid.
Transfer the array and membrane to an Agilent clamp.
Tighten the clamp to the point of resistance.
Place the clamp in a 37°C incubator for 30 minutes.
Repeat the membrane sealing procedure if running multiple arrays.
Remove the clamp from the incubator.
Remove each array from the Agilent clamp with the top slide still attached.
Submerge each array in 5 mL of pre-lysis buffer.
Gently rock the arrays in pre-lysis buffer until the top glass slide lifts off naturally.
Aspirate the pre-lysis buffer and add 5 mL of complete lysis buffer to each array.
Alternatively, prepare 5 mL of complete lysis buffer by adding 25 uL of 20% Sarkosyl and 50 uL of Beta-mercaptoethanol to pre-lysis buffer.
Rotate the arrays for 20 minutes at 50-60 rpm.
Remove the lysis buffer from each array.
Wash each array with 5 mL of hybridization buffer.
Aspirate the hybridization buffer and add another 5 mL of hybridization buffer to each array.
Rotate the arrays in hybridization buffer for 40 minutes at 50-60 rpm.
While the arrays are rocking, prepare RT master mix.
Aspirate hybridization buffer and replace with 5 mL of wash buffer.
Rock for 3 minutes.
Remove membrane with fine-tipped tweezers.
Identify the orientation of a lifter slip so that the feet are facing upwards.
Place the lifter slip(s) in a separate 4-well dish with feet oriented upwards.
Carefully transfer each array to the new dish, inverting each array so that the PDMS surface is in contact with the feet of the lift slips.
Transfer 3 mL of wash buffer to each array in the new dish.
Precisely weigh the dish containing inverted array(s) to balance the centrifuge.
Spin for 5 minutes at 1000xg.
Rinse the glass slide on the back of the array with wash buffer after centrifugation.
Invert the array and rinse the PDMS surface.
Lightly scrape the surface of the array using a microscope slide to remove any retained beads.
Remove array and rinse both sides of the lifter slips.
Collect suspended beads (10-12 mL) and transfer to a 15-mL conical tube.
Spin the conical tube(s) for 5 minutes at 1000xg.
Aspirate all liquid but 1 mL from the conical tube and transfer beads to a clean 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Rinse the 15 mL conical with 500 uL of wash buffer and add to the 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge beads for 1 minute at 1000xg.
Remove supernatant and resuspend in 250 μL of 1xMaxima RT Buffer.
Centrifuge beads for 1 minute at 1000xg.
Aspirate 1xMaxima RT buffer and resuspend beads in 200 μL of the Maxima RT Mastermix.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes with end-over-end rotation.
After 30 minutes, incubate at 52°C for 90 minutes with end-over-end rotation.
Following the RT reaction, wash beads once with 1 mL TE-TW.
Wash beads once with 1 mL TE-SDS.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL of TE-TW.
Centrifuge beads for 1 minute at 1000xg and aspirate the TE-TW solution.
Resuspend in 1 mL of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0.
Centrifuge beads again, remove supernatant and resuspend beads in 200 μL of Exonuclease I mix.
Incubate on heat block for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer to 37°C incubator for 45 minutes with end-over-end rotation.
Wash the beads once with 1 mL of TE-SDS.
Wash the beads twice with 1 mL of TE-TW each time.
Prepare the following PCR Mastermix:
Mix 25 μL of 2x KAPA HiFi Hotstart Readymix, 14.6 μL H2O, and 0.4 μL of 100 uM SMART PCR Primer to a total volume of 40 μL per reaction.
Wash beads once with 1 mL of water, pellet beads, remove supernatant, and resuspend in 500 μL of water.
Mix well to evenly resuspend beads and transfer 20 μL of beads to a separate 1.5 mL tube for counting.
Pellet the small aliquot of beads, aspirate the supernatant, and resuspend in 20 μL of bead counting solution \(10% PEG, 2.5 M NaCl).
Count the beads using a hemocytometer.
Add 40 μL of PCR Mastermix per reaction to 96-well plate.
Add 1,500 – 2,000 beads per reaction in 10 μL of water for a total volume of 50 μL per PCR reaction.
Use the following cycling conditions: 95°C for 3 minutes.
Perform 4 cycles at 98°C for 20 seconds, 65°C for 45 seconds, and 72°C for 3 minutes.
Perform 9 cycles at 98°C for 20 seconds, 67°C for 20 seconds, and 72°C for 3 minutes.
Pull PCR products for your sample in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube so that you have 14-16,000 beads/1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Purify PCR products using Ampure SPRI beads at 0.6x volumetric ratio.
Resuspend beads in a volume of water that is 10% of the starting volume.
Run a BioAnalyzer High Sensitivity Chip according to the manufacturer’s instructions using 1 ul of purified cDNA sample as input.
Proceed to library preparation or store WTA product at 4°C.
Combine 750 pg of purified cDNA with water in a total volume of 5 μL.
Add 10 μL of Nextera TD buffer to each tube.
Add 5 μL of ATM buffer to each tube (total reaction volume is now 20 μL).
Mix by pipetting approximately 5 times. Spin down the tubes.
Incubate at 55°C for 5 minutes.
Add 5 μL of Neutralization Buffer to each tube.
Mix by pipetting approximately 5 times. Spin down for 1 minute at 1000xg.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add the following components to each PCR tube in this order: 15 μL of Nextera PCR mix, 8 μL H2O, 1 μL of 10 uM P5-SMART PCR hybrid oligo, and 1 μL of 10uM Nextera N70X oligo.
Seal the reaction tubes and spin them down for 1 minute at 1000xg.
Run the following PCR program: 95°C for 30 seconds; 12 cycles of 95°C for 10 seconds, 55°C for 30 seconds, 72°C for 30 seconds; final extension at 72°C for 5 minutes, hold at 4°C.
Purify tagmentation products using Ampure SPRI beads at a 0.6x volumetric ratio.
Resuspend the purified product in 13 μL of H2O.
Run a BioAnalyzer High Sensitivity Chip according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Use 1 μl of the purified cDNA sample as input.
Make a 5 μL library pool at 4 nM as input for denaturation.
Add 5 μL of 0.2 N NaOH to the 5 μL library.
Flick to mix, then spin down and let tube sit for 5 minutes at room temperature.
After 5 minutes, add 5 μL of 0.2 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5.
Add 985 μL of HT1 Buffer to make a 1 mL, 20 pM library solution.
In a new tube, add 180 μL of the 20 pM library solution and dilute to 1.5 mL with HT1 buffer to make a 2.4 pM solution.
Follow Illumina’s guide for loading a NextSeq500 Kit.
Combine Sylgard crosslinker with Sylgard base at a 1:10 ratio and mix vigorously for 10 minutes.
Put the PDMS master mix under vacuum for 15 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Inject 10 mL of PDMS master mix into molds with mounted PDMS masters using a 10 mL syringe.
Incubate the PDMS masters at 70°C for 2.5 hours.
Remove excess PDMS from edges of the glass slide.
Use scotch tape to remove excess PDMS from the surface of the array and the glass slide.
Place clean arrays into a metal slide basket.
Rinse arrays in 100% ethanol for 10 minutes.
Plasma treat arrays on high for 5 minutes.
Submerge arrays in 350 mL of 0.05% APTES in 95% ethanol for 10 minutes.
Spin dry arrays at 500 RPM for 1 minute.
Incubate arrays at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Submerge arrays in 300 mL acetone in a glass chamber and rock until all bubbles are out of the wells.
Place arrays in 350 mL of 0.2% PDITC/10% pyridine/90% DMF solution in a glass chamber for 2 hours.
Wash arrays briefly in two different glass boxes containing 300 mL DMF each.
Dip and shake arrays in 300 mL of acetone.
Move arrays to a fresh 350 mL of acetone and rock for 20 minutes.
Spin dry arrays at 500 RPM for 1 minute.
Place arrays at 70°C for 2 hours.
Remove arrays from oven and let them sit at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Submerge array in 350 mL of 0.2% chitosan solution (pH 6.5) and incubate at 37°C for 1.5-2 hours.
Wash arrays 4 times in separate 300 mL distilled water baths.
Submerge arrays in 350 mL of 20 μg/mL poly(glutamic) acid, 2 M NaCl, and 100 mM sodium carbonate solution (pH 10.0).
Place arrays in vacuum chamber and apply house vacuum.
Rotate arrays overnight in the vacuum chamber connected to house vacuum.
Remove arrays from vacuum and rotate at 50-60 rpm for 3 hours at room temperature the following morning.
Soak arrays at 4°C for 24 hours before use.
Store arrays in poly(glutamic) acid solution at 4°C for up to 6 weeks.
Dissolve 295.4 grams of EDTA in 500 mL of water to make a 0.5 M EDTA solution.
Mix 24.625 mL pre-lysis buffer with 125 μL 10% Sarkosyl and 250 μL BME to prepare the complete lysis buffer.
Combine 10 mL 5 M NaCl, 75 μL 1 M MgCl2, 14.800 mL of PBS, and 125 μL Tween-20 to make the hybridization buffer.
Mix 10 mL 5 M NaCl, 75 μL 1 M MgCl2, 500 μL 1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.0, and 14.3 mL water to prepare the wash buffer.
Dissolve 1 gram of Chitosan in 500 mL of DI water.
Autoclave the chitosan solution (40 minutes sterilization, 20 minutes dry).
Titrate the autoclaved chitosan solution with acetic acid to lower pH to 6.5.
Add 50 mL of 5 M NaCl solution to the chitosan solution.
